glossary.def: The unit of text that an index stores, embeds and returns. It is the retrieval unit, and often also the generation unit.
Text shared between neighbouring chunks so a fact near a boundary appears whole in at least one chunk. It inflates stored tokens by size / (size - overlap).
The heading trail of a chunk, such as Returns > International > Duties, stored as metadata or prepended to the text.
Match small child chunks for precision and return the larger parent section or window for context. Also called small-to-big.
An atomic, self-contained statement of one fact, usually written by an LLM, used as a fine-grained retrieval unit.
Prepending a short LLM-written context to each chunk before embedding and BM25 indexing so ambiguous chunks can be found.
Embedding a whole document first, then pooling token embeddings per chunk span so each chunk vector carries document context.
A tree of recursively clustered and summarised chunks, searched at several levels of abstraction.
Training that front-loads information into the first dimensions of an embedding, so a prefix of the vector is still useful after truncation and re-normalising.
Storing each vector component as an 8-bit integer instead of a 32-bit float, about 4 times smaller.
Storing one bit per dimension, up to about 28 to 32 times smaller, usually combined with rescoring against original vectors.
Fetching k times a multiplier of candidates from a compressed index so they can be rescored with full vectors before returning k.
Recomputing similarity for top candidates with the original, uncompressed vectors to recover quality lost to compression.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a layered proximity graph for approximate nearest neighbour search, with parameters m, efConstruction and efSearch.
The size of the candidate list explored at query time in HNSW. Larger values raise recall and latency and need no rebuild.
Comparing the query with every vector for exact results. Simple and exact, but cost grows with the number of vectors.
A graph index designed to keep most of the data on SSD, allowing very large collections on modest memory.
Inverted file index: vectors are grouped into clusters and a query scans only the nearest few clusters (probes).
Applying a metadata filter during the vector search so the top k are drawn from allowed items, preserving recall.
Massive Text Embedding Benchmark, a multi-task leaderboard. It is a shortlist tool, because no model wins every task and it is not your corpus.
A model that embeds queries and documents with different prefixes or instructions, such as query: and passage: for E5.
Mismatch between stored vectors and query vectors after a model, version or prefix change. Vectors from different models are not comparable.

claims.text: The OpenAI and Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3 models accept up to 8,192 input tokens.
Microsoft's chunking guide suggests starting at 512 tokens (about 2,000 characters) with 25% overlap (128 tokens), and a fixed-size example of about 200 words with 10 to 15% overlap.
In one fixed-size chunking study, 64 to 128 token chunks were best for short factual answers and 512 to 1,024 token chunks helped when broader context was needed.
NVIDIA found page-level chunking best on average and 128 or 2,048 token chunks generally weaker. On FinanceBench at 1,024 tokens, 15% overlap was best of 10, 15 and 20%.

The Text Split skill has maximumPageLength default 5,000 characters (range 300 to 50,000), no overlap by default, unit characters by default and azureOpenAITokens (preview) using cl100k_base, with o200k_base not supported.
In pages mode the Text Split skill tries not to truncate a sentence, so chunks can be shorter than maximumPageLength, and maximumPageLength applies only to pages mode.
Chroma found the default RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter separators gave very short chunks and scored chunkers by token-level IoU, precision and recall.
A 2024 study found the extra compute of semantic chunking was not justified by consistent gains over fixed-size chunking.
Semantic chunking and AI image descriptions in the Content Understanding skill are opt-in preview in 2026-05-01-preview, while the skill is GA in 2026-04-01.
The Content Understanding skill chunk length defaults to 500, with a range of 300 to 50,000 characters or 100 to 8,000 tokens.
Document Intelligence v4.0 (2024-11-30) returns tables in Markdown output as HTML tables and uses the symbols ☒ and ☐ for checkboxes instead of :selected: and :unselected:.
An index projection parent id field must be Edm.String, filterable and not the document key. projectionMode is skipIndexingParentDocuments (recommended) or includeIndexingParentDocuments (default).
Projected child keys contain a random hash that changes when the parent changes, and child chunks of a deleted parent are removed only if the data source has a deletion detection policy.

Dense X Retrieval found indexing propositions beat passage-level and sentence-level units for dense retrieval, and the authors fine-tuned a Propositionizer model distilled from GPT-4 to generate them.

Contextual retrieval (Anthropic, published 2024-09-19) cut the top-20 retrieval failure rate by 35% (5.7% to 3.7%) with contextual embeddings, 49% (to 2.9%) adding contextual BM25 and 67% (to 1.9%) adding reranking.

The contextual retrieval one-time cost was estimated at 1.02 dollars per million document tokens with prompt caching, assuming 800 token chunks, 8k token documents, 50 token instructions and 100 tokens of context per chunk.
The GenAI Prompt skill is GA in Azure AI Search REST API 2026-04-01, the stable version at the check date. The newest preview is 2026-08-01-preview.
Late chunking embeds the whole text first and mean-pools token embeddings per chunk, needs a long-context embedding model and jina-embeddings-v2-base-en handles 8,192 tokens.
RAPTOR with GPT-4 raised the best result on QuALITY by 20% absolute accuracy.

text-embedding-3 default dimensions are 1,536 (small) and 3,072 (large). MTEB averages are 61.0 (ada-002), 62.3 (3-small) and 64.6 (3-large). A 256-dimension 3-large vector beat full-size ada-002 on MTEB.
MIRACL averages are 31.4 (ada-002), 44.0 (3-small) and 54.9 (3-large), and Azure OpenAI allows up to 2,048 input items per embeddings call.
Pages per dollar at about 800 tokens per page are 62,500 (3-small), 9,615 (3-large) and 12,500 (ada-002).

Cohere embed-v4.0 supports text and images with output dimensions 256, 512, 1,024 or 1,536 (default) and 128k context. embed-v5.0-pro and embed-v5.0-fast offer dimensions 256 to 2,048 (default 2,048).
The Azure retirement schedule (updated 2026-09-21) lists text-embedding-3-large, 3-small and ada-002 as retiring 2028-02-09. Embedding models cannot be upgraded in place.
MTEB v1 covers 8 task types, 58 datasets and 112 languages and no single method won every task. MMTEB has 500+ tasks and 250+ languages.

In AI Search, truncationDimension works only with scalar or binary quantization, HNSW and Edm.Half or Edm.Single fields, cannot be added to an existing field and has no portal support. Suggested value is 512, and as low as 256 for 3-large.
The Azure OpenAI embedding skill dimensions parameter defaults to the model maximum (3-large 1 to 3,072, 3-small 1 to 1,536, ada-002 fixed at 1,536) and the index field dimensions must match.

AI Search scalar quantization is int8 and 4 times smaller. Binary is up to 28 times smaller, suits dimensions above 1,024, defaultOversampling defaults to 4 and rescoring works only with HNSW. rescoreStorageMethod is preserveOriginals or discardOriginals (binary only).

In a Hugging Face experiment int8 gave 4 times less memory with about 99.3% of float32 performance, and binary gave 32 times less memory and up to 45 times faster retrieval, keeping about 96% with rescoring and 92.5% without.

E5 requires the prefixes 'query: ' and 'passage: '. BGE v1.5 uses the query instruction 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ' and no document prefix. Nomic Embed v1.5 uses 'search_document: ' and 'search_query: '.
AI Search HNSW defaults are m 4 (range 4 to 10), efConstruction 400 (100 to 1,000) and efSearch 500 (100 to 1,000), with metric cosine, dotProduct, euclidean or hamming.
pgvector HNSW defaults are m 16, ef_construction 64 and hnsw.ef_search 40. IVFFlat lists start at rows/1,000 up to 1M rows and sqrt(rows) beyond, and ivfflat.probes defaults to 1.
Qdrant default HNSW config is m 16 and ef_construct 100, full_scan_threshold is 10,000 KB, and payload indexes should be created before ingest.

AI Search vectorFilterMode has preFilter, postFilter and strictPostFilter (preview). Indexes created after about 2023-10-15 default to preFilter, older indexes default to postFilter and must be recreated to use preFilter or compression.

pgvector applies filters after the approximate scan (a 10% filter with ef_search 40 returns about 4 rows). Iterative scans since 0.8.0 use hnsw.iterative_scan strict_order or relaxed_order, bounded by hnsw.max_scan_tuples (default 20,000).

Cosmos DB for NoSQL flat indexes support up to 505 dimensions, quantizedFlat and diskANN up to 4,096, the latter two need at least 1,000 vectors or a full scan runs, and vector policies cannot be edited in place.
The AI Search vector quota is a memory quota, HNSW overhead is 1% to 20% over float32 vectors and the on-disk size of a vector index is about 3 times its in-memory size.
The DiskANN paper indexes and searches a billion-point database on one workstation with 64 GB RAM and an SSD.

pgvector indexes vector up to 2,000 dimensions, halfvec up to 4,000 and binary quantization up to 64,000. Azure pg_diskann indexes up to 16,000 dimensions from 0.6, with max_neighbors default 32 and product quantization in preview.
Pinecone namespaces per serverless index range from 100 (Starter) to 1,000,000 (Enterprise), and $in and $nin accept at most 10,000 values.
